synopsis: The existing warning fleet offers an immediate data source: vendors already log warning events and locations, and the booklet recommends starting sensor and shadow-mode logging in October 2026, continuing through winter toward a recording-and-replay pipeline by mid-2027 [f1254, f97, f7365, f64]. However, the research used no internal recordings or sensor specifications, and neither retention of replay-quality raw data nor use of existing field data to characterize sensors and site conditions was established [f7, f519, f5121]. Useful records need synchronized sensor streams, machine and braking state, calibration, environmental context and defensible ground truth; every warning and intervention should also capture operator response, task phase and whether braking was necessary [f520, f3652]. These logs can support exposure modeling and candidate-braking replay, but operator reactions censor the data, ignored-warning near misses often lack ground truth, and validation use depends on ground truth, consent and data rights [f11615, f1601, f7578, f7943, f8246]. MOSH requires 10 Hz intervention logging, seven days of onboard retention and three months on a server, with operator ID, firmware version and tamper resistance; no universal off-road event logging format was found [f2592, f2932, f2933]. Preserve raw data and model versions, verify platform compatibility with eventual sensors, and do not assume earlier recordings can replace final-hardware data: radar and ultrasonic responses cannot be recovered from camera logs [f10684, f8659, f7870, f84].
